newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians say Israel tortured, killed detainee.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say Israel tortured, killed detainee.

text.p: A Palestinian on Thursday accused Israeli police of torturing and killing his brother who was detained while trying to attend Friday prayers at Islam's third holiest shrine in Jerusalem's Old City.
Khaled Abu Daiyeh, 37, a father of five children, died in an Israeli hospital on Wednesday, his brother Nader said.

"He had been tortured and disfigured in a horrible way. He had been tortured by human beasts. You should see the body. There isn't one centimetre of his body without bruises or signs of beating," the brother told Reuters.
A Reuters cameraman who filmed Abu Daiyeh's body after it was handed to the family for burial said the skull was crushed, the chest caved in, and the hands and legs appeared broken.

Some 80 Arabs who attended Abu Daiyeh's burial on Thursday at a cemetery on Bethlehem's outskirts, under Israeli control, stoned Israeli troops in the area, witnessses said. The Israelis responded with tear gas and rubber bullets. No one was hurt.

Israeli police told Reuters that Abu Daiyeh, arrested for trying to take a policeman's gun in the Old City, was sent first to a psychiatrist. On Tuesday, he felt unwell and was taken to Jerusalem's Shaare Zedek hospital, they said.

"While they were waiting for a doctor the man got hysterical and started to attack the policeman," police spokeswoman Linda Menuhin said. Hospital guards and the police finally restrained Abu Daiyeh. He was put to bed. The next morning, Menuhin said, he was found dead by hospital staff.

A Shaare Zedek hospital spokeswoman gave Reuters a similar account. She said hospital staff tried to resuscitate Abu Daiyeh to no avail. The hospital spokeswoman refused to detail Abu Daiyeh's condition on arrival at hospital.

Abu Daiyeh, a West Bank Palestinian who had obtained Israeli citizenship after he married an Israeli Arab woman, was arrested on Friday when he did not present an identity card at the entrance to al-Aqsa mosque, his brother said.
Abu Daiyeh was injured when he scuffled with a policeman at the mosque gate and was treated at an Israeli hospital before he was jailed, where he was tortured, the brother said.
He said Abu Daiyeh was later again transferred to hospital. He spoke to his mother and family one day before he died, assuring them that he would be released soon.
"But we later were informed that he died in his hospital room," Nader said.
Palestinian human rights activists and a PLO official accused Israel of torturing Abu Daiyeh to death.

"We believe that he died as a direct result of an Israeli high court decision allowing torture," said Shawqi Issa, executive director of the Palestinian Society for the Protection of Human Rights and the Environment.
Israel's High Court in November 1996 rejected a Palestinian detainee's petition to bar Israel's Shin Bet secret service from using "physical force" while interrogating him.
